record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Hybrid MMBB and standard deep-learning pipelines
record.original_question: Can MMBB networks, whose primitives are lattice-theoretic morphological operators, be combined with standard deep-learning layers such as convolution, downsampling, upsampling, max-pooling, and ReLU to form relevant learnable pipelines?

evidence.quote: Can MMBB networks be combined with standard layers in deep learning pipelines, providing relevant learnable models?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(L, \wedge, \vee)$ be a complete lattice (e.g., the lattice of grayscale images $L = \mathbb{R}^{H\times W}$ with pointwise order). A *morphological operator* on $L$ is a mapping built from the lattice-theoretic primitives of erosion $\varepsilon_B(f)(x) = \inf_{b\in B} f(x+b)$ and dilation $\delta_B(f)(x) = \sup_{b\in B} f(x+b)$ with structuring element $B$, together with their compositions (opening, closing, etc.). A *Max-Min Basis-Based (MMBB) network* is a feed-forward parametric model whose layers are finite sup-inf (equivalently, max-min) combinations of such morphological primitives, with the structuring elements (and possibly the basis weights) treated as learnable parameters.

A *standard deep-learning layer* refers to one of: a linear convolution layer, a downsampling (strided) layer, an upsampling (e.g., transposed convolution or nearest-neighbor) layer, a max-pooling layer, or a ReLU activation $x \mapsto \max(x,0)$.

Problem. Construct hybrid feed-forward architectures that interleave MMBB layers with standard deep-learning layers (convolution, down/upsampling, max-pooling, ReLU) so that the resulting models:
(i) are end-to-end trainable by gradient-based optimization (with a well-defined notion of subgradient through the sup/inf primitives);
(ii) are universal in some precise approximation-theoretic sense on a class of image-to-image or image-to-label mappings of interest; and
(iii) on at least one standard learning task (e.g., image classification or semantic segmentation) demonstrate a quantifiable advantage—either in parameter efficiency, interpretability, or performance—over a purely convolutional baseline of comparable size.

Formalize the notion of "relevant learnable pipeline," exhibit such a construction, and prove the corresponding approximation and trainability guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works construct and train hybrid architectures combining morphological layers (erosion/dilation, max-min) with standard CNN primitives—e.g., hybrid morphological-convolutional networks for medical imaging (Frontiers in AI, 2023), "Deep Morphological Networks" (Pattern Recognition, 2020), and "Training Deep Morphological Neural Networks as Universal Approximators" (2025). These give partial positive answers (working hybrid pipelines, some universal-approximation results). However, a fully general theory matching the MMBB lattice-basis formulation with rigorous approximation and trainability guarantees and consistent empirical advantage is not established, so the question is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Hybrid morphological-convolutional neural networks for computer-aided diagnosis
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid architectures based on Morphological and Convolutional Neural Networks followed by a Random Forest classifier achieve effective performance on medical image datasets.
status_evidence.claim: Hybrid MMBB-style + CNN pipelines have been built and trained successfully on real tasks.

status_evidence.title: Deep morphological networks
status_evidence.snippet: Layers making use of morphological non-linearities are complementary to convolution layers and can be used to integrate non-linear operations and pooling into a joint operation.
status_evidence.claim: Morphological layers have been integrated with convolution and pooling in trainable deep models.

status_evidence.title: Training Deep Morphological Neural Networks as Universal Approximators
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid architectures alternating between linear and morphological layers, effectively replacing ReLU activations with morphological layers, with universal approximation results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides universal-approximation-style guarantees for hybrid morphological/linear networks.
